content.content:
# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

23	## Overview
24	
25	Interaction is the verb layer of the game: the simulation-side system that decides what a press of the single `interact` input means for the one object the player is facing, and then carries that meaning out as a real change to the world. It has a data layer and a player-facing effect, and both are stated here. **The data layer:** for each focused object and each tool in hand it *declares* a command type and a mode (`TAP`, `HOLD_CONFIRM` or `CHANNEL`); it *registers* the command types whose effect is its own (patch, salvage cut, port cap, crank, breaker, valve, door, top-up, pickup, drop, glowstick throw, field check, the friendly-harm act, cancel) and calls the Life-Support Graph's Class A mutators M6 to M9 and M11 to M13 (M10 has no MVP verb) for the player verbs V1, V3, V4, V5, V6, V8, V9 and V12, and the Class B M16 for V7 top-up (admitted to the Graph's MVP list by the 2026-10-27 user ruling X5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; it owns channel progress, the partial-progress ledger, the FULL-repair part reservation, the loose-item table, the closed domain reason set with its immediate-versus-deferred classification, and one SIM block (`interaction.state`) with one step hook (`interaction.step`). **The player-facing effect:** the player walks into their own light until a pipe, a valve, a breaker, a door or a salvageable module is close enough to touch, a prompt plate (`E · Patch`) appears only because that object is lit and in reach, and one press starts a stationary job: a linear bar fills while the tool spits and the web listens, any step away lets go of the job, and the world — the hiss thinning, the room warming, the arc stopping — answers a beat behind the player's hands. 26	
27	The one-sentence version: *Interaction is how a player puts their hands on the ship, and the price of doing so — light, noise, standing still, time — is exactly the price Pillars 3 and 4 need acting to cost.* Two rules carry the whole design. **The lit-only rule:** a verb is possible only on an object that is both in reach and lit (`in_reach` from the Player Controller GDD, `lit(ref)` from the Emitter State GDD), so going dark is a trade, never a free dodge of the web's attention. **The cost rule for truth:** a reason that depends on a module's body state (its hp, state, forced mode or served power — the channel that Pillar 4 may corrupt) is never returned at the instant of the press; the command is accepted, the full job runs, and only then does it resolve to an outcome (`nothing changed`, `not repairable`, `still hot`). An instant honest rejection on a device the player merely believes is broken or fixed would be a free lie-detector (Command & Simulation Layer CR-5, row 12), and it is forbidden by construction. Reasons that depend only on geometry, light, the actor's own stock and state, or the consequence channel (out of range, not lit, no tool, busy, obstructed) are honest and immediate.

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria

Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. - Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A

- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`

108	**Group A — Ownership, declaration, focus and the lit-only rule**
109	
110	**IA-1 Interaction is the verb layer, not a doer of everything.** Interaction (a) declares, per focused object and equipped tool, which command type and mode a press of `interact` means; (b) registers the command types whose effect is its own (IA-3); (c) owns channel progress, partial-progress persistence, pickup, drop, throw, the field check, the friendly-harm act and revive; (d) is the caller of the Graph's Class A mutators M6 to M9 and M11 to M13 (M10 has no MVP verb) for the player verbs, of the Class B M16 for V7 top-up, and of Emitter State's subject registration (E6, E7, E8) and `spawn_deployable` (E3); (e) publishes exactly three Class B mutators (`sync_section`, `place_loose`, and `open_channel` for owner-registered channels, IA-35), two read views (`focus_view`, `channel_view`) and one pure derived read (`last_salvage_T()`, IA-25), and nothing else. It never draws, never subscribes to results and never calls presentation (kernel CR-10); it uses no RNG and no wall-clock (every outcome is a deterministic function of block state, true Graph state and the tick); it holds no scene-tree reference (H10). *Decides:* advisor R1, guard G1, kernel CR-10.

An unregistered ref answers exactly as an unlit one (EM-21), so a phantom and a darkened real object are indistinguishable by design. *Why the rule exists:* it makes darkness a trade, not a free dodge of the web's attention — "unlit objects can be worked on" was rejected because working in the dark would be a free Attention dodge. 148	**IA-7 Mid-channel re-check.** Each channel re-reads `lit(target)` through the same query at the cadence of IA-14 (every `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS`, counted from the begin tick, inclusive) and aborts with cause UNLIT if it is false at a check; a dark gap shorter than the cadence is tolerated (at most `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS − 1` = 5 dark channel ticks, Emitter State AC-59b). The geometric conjuncts of `in_reach` are re-tested at the same cadence (OUT_OF_REACH). Neither re-check is tested for a record whose target class is ACTOR_SELF (exempt, IA-6); such a record's abort set is IA-14 rows 1-3 and 7-9. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated G6, GAP: the owner adds the surface the Controller's ruled behaviour needs)* The cadence tests are `e mod LIT_RECHECK_TICKS == 0` (IA-14 rows 4 to 6), and invariant I-1 (`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS mod LIT_RECHECK_TICKS == 0`; legal `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS` values 1, 2, 3 and 6) makes every block end a check tick, so no step is credited on an unlit or out-of-reach block end. The hook is `after: emitter.place`, so it reads tick T's table, not T−1's. *Decides:* R10, EM-25, the Controller's own flag at PCI:677 ("Interaction's rule to confirm" — confirmed).

| `pod_hop` (POD_CONSOLE, carry-admitted); `berth`, `unberth` (DOCK_CONSOLE) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ASK-CT-13 / ASK-CT-14 accepted, delegated G6, GAP)* | TAP (the console press, IA-40; noise: `berth` LOUD, `unberth` and `pod_hop` QUIET *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)*) | Web Map's (`{target_id}`; `{derelict_id}`; none) | **Web Map & Transit** (Designed — WM-8, WM-9) | PLAYER | Web Map's closed reason set (WM-9) |

Interaction **declares** the rows it does not register (their `verb_name_key`, mode, tool and noise class live in the declaration table) and **registers** the rest; `set_opening` alone admits `SYSTEM` origin, for a failure cascade's door close (IA-24). *Alternative considered:* one generic `interact {target, verb}` command with an internal dispatcher — rejected: one giant `validate`, mixed reason sets, per-verb age and coalescing impossible, replay logs less legible. *Stale tokens routed:* the kernel text at KRN:85 and KRN:204 lists `interact` as a command; here it is an input action only. KRN:85 (and IDB:470) also list `use_item`, which no GDD registers: Suit registers exactly `equip_tool` and states `use_item` is not its command (SE-40, AC-SE-39), so it is removed from this table and routed to the kernel and Item DB owners as a stale token; the suppressant's effect verb (Suit's `consume_charge`) is declared here when Attention or Horror register it, and no MVP row exists (Cross-References). *Decides:* R1, R2, PC-6, LS-22, Controller acceptance at PCI:969.

**IA-4 Focus is the Controller's; Interaction re-validates; no rule branches on device.** The Adapter chooses exactly one focused object by the aim-weighted score (`FOCUS_AIM_WEIGHT`, `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN`; ties go to the smaller aim angle, then the smaller entity id; Controller D.9) and submits the *declared* type with that ref. The simulation never computes a score; it re-validates the chosen target with `in_reach` (`REACH_PX`, `REACH_HALF_ANGLE_DEG`, `COS2_REACH`; cited, not restated) and `lit`. There is no pick-under-cursor path on any device. A gamepad user who never touches the right stick focuses by facing (aim follows movement until the first right-stick input, PC-4/5); `interact` with no focus is an Adapter no-op (no command, no pre-play; the Adapter plays only its local `cue_input_ignored`) — except the self-target: the Controller nominates the actor's own suit as the focus when the equipped tool has an ACTOR_SELF row and no world candidate is focusable (PC-6), and the press then submits `begin_patch {own PlayerId}` (IA-17; `focus_view.self_target`, IA-41) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6, GAP: the owner adds the surface the Controller's ruled behaviour needs)*. No Interaction rule reads the input device, hold-versus-toggle or tap-to-confirm policy (Adapter policy, PC-7 and PC-13); lint: `assets/data/interaction/verbs` takes no sanity, Attention, rhythm, breach or device input. *Decides:* PC-6, R26, T8.

**IA-5 One contextual action: `select_verb`.** Given the focused object's classes and the tool in hand (Suit's `tool_in_hand`, Suit & Equipment, Designed — SE-40), the declaration row is chosen by: (1) the rows whose `tool_required` equals the tool in hand, lowest `priority` first; else (2) the bare-hand rows, lowest `priority` first; else (3) the lowest-`priority` row of the class, shown with its tool glyph and answered `NO_TOOL` on press. The choice is a function of (object classes, tool in hand, the `eligible` predicate) only — **never of hp, state, forced mode or served power** (IA-11). While the actor carries a module, the only selectable rows are `drop` placement and the declared carry-admitted rows (`admitted_while_carrying`: `install_module` on a HARDPOINT whose `compatible_defs(h)` lists the carried instance's def, `pod_hop` on the POD_CONSOLE, and V4 `set_opening` on a door face; IA-28) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; any other world target while carrying is shown no prompt at all. *Example:* a scrubber with the welder in hand selects V1 `begin_patch`; with the cutter in hand it selects V8 `begin_cut`; with bare hands row (3) selects V1 and shows the welder glyph — the press answers `NO_TOOL`. ACTOR_SELF rows are selected by tier (1) only (the exact tool in hand): tiers (2) and (3) never apply to ACTOR_SELF, so a player without the welder in hand sees no self plate and no `NEEDS_TOOL` variant for it. The Adapter evaluates this same pure data lookup (the declaration table, IA-2) with class ACTOR_SELF and Suit's `tool_in_hand` to decide whether to nominate the self-target (IA-4). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6, GAP: the owner adds the surface the Controller's ruled behaviour needs)* *Alternatives considered:* hide the verb without the tool (the player never learns it exists); auto-equip the right tool (removes a Suit decision and makes `equip_tool` pointless). *Decides:* R11, HR-14 (one contextual action), D10.

**IA-6 Act only on what is lit (`act_gate`).** `act_gate(o) = in_reach(o) AND lit(o)`, where `in_reach` is the Controller's integer predicate (itself including the lit conjunct) and `lit` is Emitter State's hysteresis bit (`LIT_ON_PM`, `LIT_OFF_PM`, no dwell). Every PLAYER-origin Interaction command whose declaration is not exempt checks `act_gate` in `validate`, against the exposure table committed at tick T−1 (EM-25). The exceptions are exactly three, plus the actor verbs that are not object verbs: `drop` of the carried module, `toggle_beam`, and the inspect card of an already-lit instrument (PC-6); `throw_glowstick` is an actor verb like `toggle_beam` and needs no lit target (IA-29); and **the self-patch is an actor verb too**: `begin_patch` on object class `ACTOR_SELF` (IA-17) targets the actor's own suit, so there is no object to light and no reach to test; its declaration row has `exempt(row) = 1`, `validate` skips both `in_reach` and `lit` for it, and an ACTOR_SELF row can produce neither `OUT_OF_RANGE` nor `NOT_LIT`. This is not a fourth object exception: the object list stays exactly three (`drop`, `toggle_beam`, the inspect card of an already-lit instrument), and the pod-console refusal below is unchanged. The dark self-patch is still priced, so it is not a free Attention dodge (Pillar 3): TOOL noise on every accrued tick (IA-33), 180 stationary ticks (`PATCH_CHANNEL_TICKS`) and the welder in hand. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated G6, GAP: the owner adds the surface the Controller's ruled behaviour needs)* **No fourth exception for the pod console (refused, stated here):** Web Map's ASK-I2 and Boarding's ASK-BS-I3 ask that `pod_hop` at the CONSOLE be exempt from the lit condition; the three exceptions are the Controller's PC-6 list (PCI:127) and IA-17 already refuses a fourth, so `pod_hop`, `berth` and `unberth` stay lit-gated (on both the POD_CONSOLE and the DOCK_CONSOLE subject, IA-40), and the hop stays available by content, not by exemption: the docked pod's dock-room prop carries a small self-powered status glow that counts as an ordinary lit fixture (not a fourth `act_gate` exception), so `pod_hop`'s lit gate is always satisfied at the console and a `NOT_LIT` at a dock console is a content defect, not a state (Open Question 31, resolved) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2, Web Map option (B); this refusal STANDS. The self-powered fixture class (Emitter State EM-3 / EM-11), the placement rule and lint in every dock room (Derelict Authoring), the art-director's luminance separation from the visible-unknown lamp and Web Map accepting ASK-BS-W3 are the other owners' sides; Boarding's BS-19 invariant is owned jointly: Web Map and Emitter State guarantee the glow, Authoring lints its placement)*. An unregistered ref answers exactly as an unlit one (EM-21), so a phantom and a darkened real object are indistinguishable by design. *Why the rule exists:* it makes darkness a trade, not a free dodge of the web's attention — "unlit objects can be worked on" was rejected because working in the dark would be a free Attention dodge. Pillars: **P3** (every action spends exposure) and **P4** (reaching for a phantom finds nothing). *Decides:* PC-6, EM-21/22/25, F2 (the composite is registered as a formula, D.2).

**IA-7 Mid-channel re-check.** Each channel re-reads `lit(target)` through the same query at the cadence of IA-14 (every `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS`, counted from the begin tick, inclusive) and aborts with cause UNLIT if it is false at a check; a dark gap shorter than the cadence is tolerated (at most `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS − 1` = 5 dark channel ticks, Emitter State AC-59b). The geometric conjuncts of `in_reach` are re-tested at the same cadence (OUT_OF_REACH). Neither re-check is tested for a record whose target class is ACTOR_SELF (exempt, IA-6); such a record's abort set is IA-14 rows 1-3 and 7-9. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated G6, GAP: the owner adds the surface the Controller's ruled behaviour needs)* The cadence tests are `e mod LIT_RECHECK_TICKS == 0` (IA-14 rows 4 to 6), and invariant I-1 (`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS mod LIT_RECHECK_TICKS == 0`; legal `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS` values 1, 2, 3 and 6) makes every block end a check tick, so no step is credited on an unlit or out-of-reach block end. The hook is `after: emitter.place`, so it reads tick T's table, not T−1's. *Decides:* R10, EM-25, the Controller's own flag at PCI:677 ("Interaction's rule to confirm" — confirmed).

298	**IA-33 Noise.** The declaration carries `noise_class` in {QUIET, TOOL, LOUD}. As channel owner, Interaction calls Attention's intake `push_stimulus(NOISE, source_ref, class)` once per *accrued* channel tick for TOOL-class verbs (cutter, welder, crank, scanner) and one-shot LOUD events at cut completion, seam-cut DONE (Assembly's `begin_seam_cut`, MSA-29), vent apply, throw landing and the `berth` apply (the pod console's `berth`, ruled LOUD; `unberth` and `pod_hop` stay QUIET) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)* *(Attention System, Designed — AT-3: the API and the class set {QUIET, TOOL, LOUD} confirmed)*. A tick that aborts before accrual pushes nothing. Units are Attention's; the Controller's `NOISE_PER_TICK` (walk, run, carry) is cited, never restated. A breaker close pushes nothing (the Graph's inrush is Attention's power stimulus through `power_use`); a door motor pushes nothing. Interaction states three relations Attention's units must satisfy, or the verbs become free or absurd: the TOOL-class per-tick unit lies between 2 and 6 so a 180-tick patch integrates to at least twice the walking noise of the same time and no more than 1.5 times the running noise; a LOUD one-shot is at least 30 ticks of the TOOL unit; and `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS ≤ 2 × TAU_ATT_TICKS` (IA-16) — Attention accepts all three (registry `noise_unit_relations` IR-1 to IR-3: `2 ≤ U_TOOL ≤ 6`, `U_LOUD ≥ 30 × U_TOOL`, `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS ≤ 2 × TAU_ATT_TICKS`). Attention never reads Audio (IDX:34). **Pillar 3 trace (ruled: it does not depend on sparks).** The Pillar 3 price of any channel is carried by two things that exist regardless of how Open Question 18 resolves: the target must be lit (IA-6, IA-7), so the job is done in light the web can see through Emitter State's exposure, and a dark job is impossible but for the three listed exceptions; and the tool's TOOL-class noise push on every accrued tick (above). Weld and cut sparks are non-emissive at MVP (art-director AD-6: no Light2D, not an Emitter State emitter), so the trace never rests on them. The decision is explicitly reversible: if playtest shows welding does not feel costly to the web, Emitter State may register a short-lived spark emitter at the tool-grip anchor; that only adds a cost and changes no Interaction rule, formula or acceptance row except the spark palette lint (R-7). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **the price needs a tell, and the tell has an owner.** A TOOL push that nothing answers is a hidden stat, which Pillar 3 forbids. The tell of Interaction's noise is Attention's (its noise-driven attention tell and consequence, the web's answer, AT-3 and its tell outputs) voiced by Adaptive Audio (cue keys owned there); Interaction pushes the class and nothing else, and adds no reaction of its own. The test is AC-IA-136, a playtest row: after a TOOL push a consequence is perceived within about 10 s and named by most testers. A note on the trade: the scanner dominates hand-checking as a way to resolve a hallucination, because it costs less than a whole repair bar; that is accepted and stated in Player Fantasy: the hands answer the world, the scanner answers Sanity (Open Question 32).)* *Decides:* R16, P3, PCI D.17 / Open Question 8.

300	**IA-34 Contention.** One in-progress job per `(subject_ref, verb class)`; the verb classes are REPAIR (V1, PATCH and FULL), SALVAGE, CAP, CRANK, CHECK, WELD and ACTOR_ACT (harm, revive). WELD covers Assembly's `begin_weld` and `begin_seam_cut`, keyed on the host socket Assembly derives (Modular Ship Assembly D.3), so the two sockets of one pair contend as one subject (MSA-37, ASK I1 (x)). A second seat gets immediate `BUSY` — the crewmate's body and beam at the object are the visible reason. Solo: a second `begin_*` during a channel is `BUSY`; nothing queues (PCI:84). The Item DB's AC-89 (two seats, one kit each, same FULL repair on the same step → exactly one kit spent, the second job answered `BLOCKED` with no part consumed) is satisfied in intent: the second seat's begin is `BUSY` at `validate`, makes no reservation, and exactly one part is spent. 302	**IA-35 Cancel across owners.** `cancel_channel` is Interaction's one cancel type (KRN:85) and cancels whatever `controller.state.channel_ref` names, stored as `(owner_system, channel_id)`. Which route clears the S4 WARN was Open Question 30, since ruled by the user (D37 route (a), below).)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R21: the stale owed-decision marker is closed; D37 is the decision)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: ruled, D37 route (a), see below.)* **The legal loaded sets are Derelict Authoring's** (registry `legal_loaded_sets`, confirmed by Web Map WM-24): `S_int` = F + L_seed + C is 70 / 102 / 113 / 113 / 145 for S0 to S4, and S4 `{home+B, A}` exceeds `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` by 25 (OQ-DA-20) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: Derelict Authoring L_seed B 3, one loose placement fewer)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D37, route (a) of Open Question 30 is ruled, so the former lint "ERROR above 120 on S0 to S3 and WARN with the shortfall on S4" is superseded: the lint is per registration window, below, and the S4 WARN is retired. The loaded-set figures stay as Derelict Authoring's registered upper bound. At S4 the loaded `S_total` = 145 + 24 + 4 + 2 = 175 ≤ `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` 192 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: Derelict Authoring L_seed B 3, one loose placement fewer)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*, so nothing fails dark, and no nearest-subject cull exists; "resolved by proximity" in Boarding ASK-BS-I5 (d) means focus, not registration.)* **Registration window (D37, user ruling: register subjects by body adjacency or proximity, not by loaded section).** `sync_section` still runs at the same callers and now maintains only the section's **candidate table** (declared interactables from Layout's `subject_anchors`, the loose items placed in it, its stubs: data, not Emitter subjects); a candidate becomes a subject (Emitter `register_subject`, E6) only while it is inside the **registration window** `W` of a bound body: the rooms (`room_id`, from `subject_anchors`) whose hop distance from a bound body's current room is at most `SUBJECT_WINDOW_HOPS` ([PLACEHOLDER — derive at spike], provisional 2), a hop being one door, seam hatch or dock link, counted across welded seams and docks. Items the player creates (drops, salvage yield) sit at the player's feet and so are always in `W`. A subject outside `W` is unregistered and answers exactly as an unlit one (EM-21), which is correct because `in_reach` cannot be true for it; AC-IA-144 asserts that every candidate in reach from every walkable foot position is in `W`. `W` is a function of body positions, a SIM fact, so it is deterministic; `post_restore` rebuilds it from the restored positions, reading the restored `pos_curr` of `body.state` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, and persists no new state. **The budget is re-scoped** to the window: `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` 120 and `PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE` 24 keep their values and the I-7 relation, and the lint is `W_int(p) = F + L_seed + C` summed over the rooms of `W` and its hysteresis ring (hop distance up to `SUBJECT_WINDOW_HOPS + 1`), at most `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` at every authored body position `p` of each registered loaded set (D.10). Because a window is a subset of its loaded set, `S_int` of `legal_loaded_sets` (70 / 102 / 113 / 113 / 145) is an upper bound on `W_int`: S0 to S3 pass by construction (113 ≤ 120), S4 passes iff every window excludes at least 25 of its 145 subjects, and the runtime total never exceeds the loaded sum (175 ≤ 192) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: Derelict Authoring L_seed B 3, one loose placement fewer)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* The S4 verdict depends on room-level subject counts that Derelict Authoring and Layout own, so it is measured, not assumed ([PLACEHOLDER — derive at spike]). A runtime overflow (E6 returns false and the object fails dark, which reads as a hallucination) is a content defect, counted `IA_SUBJECT_OVERFLOW`, never a gameplay state. A `drop` or `place_loose` needs a headroom read from Emitter State (provisional name `subject_headroom()`); a player `drop` with no headroom is refused `OBSTRUCTED`, so a dropped item can never be left unregistered and un-pickable. **Group G — Cross-cutting rules**

**IA-33 Noise.** The declaration carries `noise_class` in {QUIET, TOOL, LOUD}. As channel owner, Interaction calls Attention's intake `push_stimulus(NOISE, source_ref, class)` once per *accrued* channel tick for TOOL-class verbs (cutter, welder, crank, scanner) and one-shot LOUD events at cut completion, seam-cut DONE (Assembly's `begin_seam_cut`, MSA-29), vent apply, throw landing and the `berth` apply (the pod console's `berth`, ruled LOUD; `unberth` and `pod_hop` stay QUIET) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)* *(Attention System, Designed — AT-3: the API and the class set {QUIET, TOOL, LOUD} confirmed)*. A tick that aborts before accrual pushes nothing. Units are Attention's; the Controller's `NOISE_PER_TICK` (walk, run, carry) is cited, never restated. A breaker close pushes nothing (the Graph's inrush is Attention's power stimulus through `power_use`); a door motor pushes nothing. Interaction states three relations Attention's units must satisfy, or the verbs become free or absurd: the TOOL-class per-tick unit lies between 2 and 6 so a 180-tick patch integrates to at least twice the walking noise of the same time and no more than 1.5 times the running noise; a LOUD one-shot is at least 30 ticks of the TOOL unit; and `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS ≤ 2 × TAU_ATT_TICKS` (IA-16) — Attention accepts all three (registry `noise_unit_relations` IR-1 to IR-3: `2 ≤ U_TOOL ≤ 6`, `U_LOUD ≥ 30 × U_TOOL`, `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS ≤ 2 × TAU_ATT_TICKS`). Attention never reads Audio (IDX:34). **Pillar 3 trace (ruled: it does not depend on sparks).** The Pillar 3 price of any channel is carried by two things that exist regardless of how Open Question 18 resolves: the target must be lit (IA-6, IA-7), so the job is done in light the web can see through Emitter State's exposure, and a dark job is impossible but for the three listed exceptions; and the tool's TOOL-class noise push on every accrued tick (above). Weld and cut sparks are non-emissive at MVP (art-director AD-6: no Light2D, not an Emitter State emitter), so the trace never rests on them. The decision is explicitly reversible: if playtest shows welding does not feel costly to the web, Emitter State may register a short-lived spark emitter at the tool-grip anchor; that only adds a cost and changes no Interaction rule, formula or acceptance row except the spark palette lint (R-7). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **the price needs a tell, and the tell has an owner.** A TOOL push that nothing answers is a hidden stat, which Pillar 3 forbids. The tell of Interaction's noise is Attention's (its noise-driven attention tell and consequence, the web's answer, AT-3 and its tell outputs) voiced by Adaptive Audio (cue keys owned there); Interaction pushes the class and nothing else, and adds no reaction of its own. The test is AC-IA-136, a playtest row: after a TOOL push a consequence is perceived within about 10 s and named by most testers. A note on the trade: the scanner dominates hand-checking as a way to resolve a hallucination, because it costs less than a whole repair bar; that is accepted and stated in Player Fantasy: the hands answer the world, the scanner answers Sanity (Open Question 32).)* *Decides:* R16, P3, PCI D.17 / Open Question 8.

**IA-34 Contention.** One in-progress job per `(subject_ref, verb class)`; the verb classes are REPAIR (V1, PATCH and FULL), SALVAGE, CAP, CRANK, CHECK, WELD and ACTOR_ACT (harm, revive). WELD covers Assembly's `begin_weld` and `begin_seam_cut`, keyed on the host socket Assembly derives (Modular Ship Assembly D.3), so the two sockets of one pair contend as one subject (MSA-37, ASK I1 (x)). A second seat gets immediate `BUSY` — the crewmate's body and beam at the object are the visible reason. Solo: a second `begin_*` during a channel is `BUSY`; nothing queues (PCI:84). The Item DB's AC-89 (two seats, one kit each, same FULL repair on the same step → exactly one kit spent, the second job answered `BLOCKED` with no part consumed) is satisfied in intent: the second seat's begin is `BUSY` at `validate`, makes no reservation, and exactly one part is spent. The token differs from AC-89's wording because commands dispatch sequentially, so the second begin is rejected before it could be Applied; routed to the Item DB owner as a wording refresh. As belt and braces for Vertical Slice B (should the exclusion ever be relaxed), the hook processes seats in ascending PlayerId, and a FULL step on a subject already at `hp = hp_cap = HP_FULL` is skipped: the job resolves `PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)` and consumes no part. Dispatch is sequential by kernel rule: CR-2's P2 row (KRN:63, "per command in order: authority check -> validate -> apply or reject") and KRN:69 ("P2 commands see earlier P2 effects in the same tick"). *Decides:* R21, IDB-20(7), PC-2.

**IA-35 Cancel across owners.** `cancel_channel` is Interaction's one cancel type (KRN:85) and cancels whatever `controller.state.channel_ref` names, stored as `(owner_system, channel_id)`. Every channel record lives in `interaction.state`, whoever registered the verb: Assembly's `begin_weld` and `begin_seam_cut` applies create theirs through Interaction's Class B `open_channel(seat, owner_system, verb_id, target_ref, duration_ticks)` (registry: `open_channel`; Modular Ship Assembly, Designed — MSA-30, C4), which writes the IA-14 record with that `owner_system` (consulting the IA-16 ledger for `resume_offset`, so an aborted weld or cut resumes inside `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS`, AC-MSA-50) and changes nothing else (the caller's apply calls the Controller's 4-argument `set_channel_ref` itself, with its own `face_octant`) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6/G1, CONFLICT)*. `cancel_channel` therefore ends any record `ABORT(CANCELLED)` in P2, so no accrual happens that tick; Assembly publishes no cancel (registry `assembly_commands`: `abort_channel` absent by decision). At an ASSEMBLY-owned DONE Interaction applies nothing but the `channel_ref` clear and the ledger delete (IA-14 row 9); Assembly's `assembly.step`, ordered after `interaction.step`, reads the DONE handoff in `channel_view` and submits its own SYSTEM-origin completion. The Adapter never learns the owner (the same principle as "the Adapter never chooses the verb"). *Alternatives considered:* each owner registers its own cancel — the Adapter would have to know the owner; an Assembly-published `abort_channel(actor)` (R22's provisional route) — refused by Assembly (MSA-30) and closed. *Decides:* R22, PC-6, MSA-30.

They are budgeted as the term `Y` of D.10 and share the player reserve, `P + Y ≤ PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE`; no new constant is added and the I-7 sum is unchanged. The S4 figure is re-checked in D.10. Which route clears the S4 WARN was Open Question 30, since ruled by the user (D37 route (a), below).)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R21: the stale owed-decision marker is closed; D37 is the decision)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: ruled, D37 route (a), see below.)* **The legal loaded sets are Derelict Authoring's** (registry `legal_loaded_sets`, confirmed by Web Map WM-24): `S_int` = F + L_seed + C is 70 / 102 / 113 / 113 / 145 for S0 to S4, and S4 `{home+B, A}` exceeds `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` by 25 (OQ-DA-20) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: Derelict Authoring L_seed B 3, one loose placement fewer)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D37, route (a) of Open Question 30 is ruled, so the former lint "ERROR above 120 on S0 to S3 and WARN with the shortfall on S4" is superseded: the lint is per registration window, below, and the S4 WARN is retired. Source: design/gdd/interaction-system.md (Layer Feature, MVP, 41 rules IA-1..IA-41, 14 formulas).

| Req ID | Requirement | Domain | GDD anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| TR-interact-001 | Interaction registers one command type per verb (begin_patch, begin_cut, begin_cap, begin_crank, cancel_channel, set_breaker, set_valve, top_up, set_opening, pickup, drop, throw_glowstick, field_check, begin_harm, begin_revive), each with its own validate, reason subset, max_age_ticks 120, coalesce NONE, actor_binding OWNED_BY_ISSUER with actor_source body.state, allowed_origins {PLAYER} and not allowed_when_paused; `interact` is an input action, never a command type. | Core | IA-3 |
| TR-interact-002 | Command payloads are primitives only (a registered subject ref, a PlayerId, or aim_angle for throw_glowstick and the closed check_kind {SCAN}); a payload never carries a believed state, direction, verb choice or kind. | Core | IA-3 |
| TR-interact-003 | Only set_opening admits SYSTEM origin (failure-cascade door close); all other Interaction commands are PLAYER origin. | Core | IA-3, IA-24 |
| TR-interact-004 | The verb declaration table is data, one row per (object class, tool requirement) under assets/data/interaction/verbs/, and takes no sanity, Attention, rhythm, breach or device input (data-load lint); adding a verb is one data row, one handler and one registration line with an empty Adapter diff. | Data | IA-2, IA-4 |
| TR-interact-005 | select_verb is a pure function of (object classes, tool in hand, eligible predicate) and never of hp, state, forced mode or served power. | Core | IA-5, IA-11 |
| TR-interact-006 | Every non-exempt PLAYER command validates act_gate(o) = in_reach(o) AND lit(o) against the exposure table committed at tick T-1; exemptions are exactly drop, toggle_beam, the inspect card of an already-lit instrument (plus actor verbs throw_glowstick and the ACTOR_SELF self-patch); an unregistered ref answers exactly as an unlit one. | Core | IA-6, D.2 |
| TR-interact-007 | A reason depending on module body state (hp, state, forced mode, served power) is never returned at press time: the command is Applied, the full channel runs, and only then resolves to an outcome (NOTHING_TO_REPAIR, NOT_REPAIRABLE, STILL_HOT); immediate reasons are limited to geometry, light, the actor's own stock/state and the consequence channel. | Core | Overview cost rule for truth, IA-10..IA-13, D.3 |
| TR-interact-008 | A channel is one record per seat in interaction.state, created by the verb's apply in P2 together with the Controller's set_channel_ref and advanced only by hook interaction.step, accruing from e=1 to D, with D mod GRAPH_STEP_TICKS(6) == 0 for every *_CHANNEL_TICKS (lint) and seats processed in ascending PlayerId. | Threading/Timing | IA-14, I-2 |
| TR-interact-009 | interaction.step runs `after: emitter.place` (reads tick T's exposure table) and re-checks lit and in_reach every LIT_RECHECK_TICKS (legal values 1,2,3,6; GRAPH_STEP_TICKS mod LIT_RECHECK_TICKS == 0) so no step is credited on an unlit or out-of-reach block end. | Threading/Timing | IA-7, I-1 |
| TR-interact-010 | Every Interaction predicate and formula is integer-only, uses no RNG and no wall-clock, reads body.state.pos and the Emitter State table, and no physics query (Godot Physics 2D) is permitted anywhere in the system; throws use an integer direction table with no runtime trigonometry. | Core | IA-1, Dependencies engine note, D.4 |
| TR-interact-011 | Interaction holds no scene-tree reference and never draws, subscribes to results or calls presentation; it exposes only the read views focus_view and channel_view. | Core | IA-1, IA-41 |
| TR-interact-012 | One in-progress job per (subject_ref, verb class) with classes REPAIR, SALVAGE, CAP, CRANK, CHECK, WELD, ACTOR_ACT; a second begin gets immediate BUSY, nothing queues, and a FULL step on a subject already at hp = hp_cap = HP_FULL resolves PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR) consuming no part. | Core | IA-34 |
| TR-interact-013 | cancel_channel cancels whatever controller.state.channel_ref names as (owner_system, channel_id); all channel records live in interaction.state regardless of owner, and owner-registered verbs (Assembly begin_weld/begin_seam_cut) create theirs via Class B open_channel(seat, owner_system, verb_id, target_ref, duration_ticks). | Core | IA-35 |
| TR-interact-014 | interaction.state is a SIM block, persist true, persist_scope WORLD, scope SHARED with per-seat records keyed by PlayerId (never transport peer id), repl_hint SHARED_SUMMARY, schema_version 1, restore_after [layout.state, controller.state, graph.state, body.state, emitter.state]. | Save/Load | IA-36 |

## Public surface
- Commands (registered by Interaction): `begin_patch`, `begin_cut`, `begin_cap`, `begin_crank`, `cancel_channel`, `set_breaker`, `set_valve`, `top_up`, `set_opening` (PLAYER and SYSTEM), `pickup`, `drop`, `throw_glowstick`, `field_check`, `begin_harm`, `begin_revive` (dormant).
- Declared but registered by others: `begin_weld`, `begin_seam_cut`, `install_module` (Assembly); `set_switch`, `toggle_beam` (Emitter State); `equip_tool` (Suit); `pod_hop`, `berth`, `unberth` (Web Map).
- Class B mutators: `sync_section(section_id)`, `place_loose`, `open_channel(seat, owner_system, verb_id, target_ref, duration_ticks)`.
- Read views: `focus_view(seat)` (focus_ref, anchor_o, self_target, verb_id, mode, duration_class, part_tell, tool_required, prompt_state, verb_name_key, glyph_action, focus_seq, press_blocked_moving, carry_state, drop_available, drop_anchor_o); `channel_view(seat)` (owner, verb_id, state, transition_seq, result_seq, progress_pm, length_class, outcome, abort_cause, ended_by, DONE handoff, last_result, prev_result).
- Pure derived read: `last_salvage_T()`.
- SIM block `interaction.state` (WORLD, persisted) and step hook `interaction.step`.
- Declaration data table under `assets/data/interaction/verbs/`; knobs under `assets/data/interaction/`.
- Diagnostic counters `IA_*` (e.g. IA_SUBJECT_OVERFLOW, IA_CANCEL_NOOP, IA_GRACE_EVICT) registered under `diag_panel_contract`.
- Closed restore-failure reason `INTERACTION_RESTORE_LOOSE_INSTANCE`.

## Consumes
- Command & Simulation Layer (Hard): command registration CR-4, validate/apply in P2 CR-2, result events CR-5, WriteScope/mutators CR-9, block/hook registries CR-3/CR-8, pause CR-16, `ticks_for_seconds`.
- Player Controller & Input (Hard): focus and declared-type submit (PC-6), `controller.state` reads (octant, loco_state, carry_ref, channel_ref), `in_reach`, hook `controller.step`, mutators `set_channel_ref`/`clear_channel_ref`/`set_carry_ref`/`clear_carry_ref`, `input_view` (via HUD).
- Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query (Hard): `lit(ref)`, `lux(ref)`, E6/E7/E8 subject registration, E3 `spawn_deployable`, hook `emitter.place`, `subject_headroom()`.
- Life-Support Graph (Hard): Class A M6-M9, M11-M13 with `check_*`, Class B M16, `node()`/`edge()` reads, `open_ends(node_id)`, `switch_pos`, `opening(edge_id)`.
- Item & Module Database (Soft): `ToolDef.verbs[]`, `salvageable`, `repair_part_for`, `parts_per_full`, `salvage_yield`, `to_array`/`from_array`/`validate_instance`/`fresh_instance`.
- Suit & Equipment (Hard): `tool_in_hand`, `stowed_count`, `can_stow`, `spend_stowed`, `add_stowed`, `reserve_stowed`/`release_stowed`/`consume_reserved`, `set_carried`/`release_carried`, `replace_tool`, `credit_reserve`/`credit_cell`, `patch_integrity`, `apply_suit_damage`, `revive`.
- Sanity & Hallucination Rules (Hard): `actor_sanity_below_harm_threshold`, `record_falsification`, `record_harm_event`.
- Ship Section & Layout Data Model (Hard): `subject_anchors`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `clip_to_footprints`, `floor_tile_at`, `loose_slots`, door `area_max`/travel time, `layout.state`.
- Ship Body & Interior Physics (Hard for V4): `foot_boxes(body_id)`, body-local foot origin, `body.state` pos.
- Attention System (Soft): `push_stimulus(NOISE, source_ref, class)`.
- Modular Ship Assembly: `weld_offer`, `seam_cut_offer`; Web Map & Transit / Chart Table: `console_ready(role)`, `berthed_present()`, `pick_glyph_key`; Derelict Authoring: seeded placements, `legal_loaded_sets`.
